verdict.headline: This agreement exposes you to unlimited liability and imposes high-risk renewal, foreign law, and missing data protection terms.
summary: Your liability is completely uncapped while the vendor caps its liability to just one month of fees.
The agreement applies US Delaware law even though both parties are based in Malaysia and Singapore.
It requires a long 90-day cancellation notice to avoid automatic renewal, and key protections like data protection are absent.

findings.title: Uncapped customer liability
findings.quote: The Customer shall be liable without limit for any loss suffered by the Vendor.
findings.why_risky: You are exposed to unlimited financial risk for any loss the vendor claims, while the vendor enjoys a tight liability limit.
findings.standard: Liability caps should be mutual and generally capped at the fees paid or payable in the prior 12 months.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the limitation of liability mutual, set the cap at the fees paid in the previous 12 months for both parties, and apply the same exclusions and carve-outs to both.

findings.title: Vendor liability cap is too low
findings.quote: The Vendor's total liability is limited to the fees paid in the one month before the claim.
findings.why_risky: A cap of only one month of fees means you cannot recover meaningful losses if the vendor fails or causes damage.
findings.standard: The market standard is a mutual cap equal to 12 months of fees.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the limitation of liability mutual, set the cap at the fees paid in the previous 12 months for both parties, and apply the same exclusions and carve-outs to both.

findings.title: Long notice window for automatic renewal
findings.quote: This Agreement renews automatically for successive 12 month terms unless the Customer gives 90 days written notice.
findings.why_risky: A 90-day notice window makes it easy to miss the cancellation deadline and get locked in for another full year.
findings.standard: Notice to prevent automatic renewal should be 30 days (or at most 60 days) with a reminder from the vendor.
findings.suggested_ask: Please change renewal to 12-month periods with 30 days' notice to stop renewal, and have the vendor send a written reminder 60 days before the renewal date.

findings.title: Distant foreign governing law
findings.quote: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
findings.why_risky: Resolving disputes under Delaware law would require expensive US lawyers and procedures even though both businesses operate in Southeast Asia.
findings.standard: Contracts between Malaysian and Singaporean businesses should use Malaysian or Singapore law and local courts.
findings.suggested_ask: Please make the agreement subject to Malaysian law (or Singapore law) and the courts of Kuala Lumpur (or Singapore), where both parties operate.

missing_clauses.title: Personal Data Protection Clause
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The vendor provides cloud bookkeeping and handles your financial and personal data, but there are no terms requiring data security, breach notifications, or PDPA compliance.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please add a data protection clause: processing only on our instructions, reasonable security, breach notice within 48 hours, approved subcontractors, and return or deletion of data at the end.

missing_clauses.title: Confidentiality Clause
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no obligation for the vendor to keep your business records, financial figures, or accounting details confidential.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please make the confidentiality obligations mutual, with the standard exceptions, lasting at least three years after the agreement ends, and require our consent before naming us publicly.

missing_clauses.title: Termination and Data Return
missing_clauses.why_it_matters: The contract lacks clear termination rights for breach and provides no procedure for retrieving or exporting your bookkeeping data upon exit.
missing_clauses.suggested_ask: Please give both parties the same notice period, allow 30 days to fix a breach, and add a 30-day window to export our data on termination.

disclaimer: This is an automated review to help you prepare. It is not legal advice.
